baseline: architect review of the intermediate Home implementation
observed: Home requests the admin-scoped TMDB token endpoint for every signed-in person, including sessions without settings permission or recent local-password proof.
Every failed TMDB token read is currently treated as configured, so permission, assurance, route, and server failures all create a false completed setup step.
The setup workspace and its settings links are rendered to household members who cannot open those settings pages.
target: Read the masked TMDB setup state only when the current person has settings permission and the session meets the server's admin-route assurance rule.
Treat an unavailable protected read as unknown and label it Check TMDB connection; never count it as complete.
Show the administrative setup workspace only to people with settings permission, while keeping the normal Home activity and empty-library experience available to household members.
contract_findings: GET /health and GET /health/checks do not include TMDB credential readiness.
GET /settings/tmdb-token is the existing frontend contract for masked readiness, but it is admin-scoped and protected by recent local-password assurance for browser sessions.
No backend or API contract change is required for the safe frontend behavior.
boundaries: Do not read, log, capture, or expose token or configuration values.
Preserve the existing Home composition, operational data, and non-settings navigation.
